nodes.name: Hydrothermal Synthesis of NiFe LDH
nodes.procedure: A simple one-step hydrothermal method was carried out to synthesize NiFe LDH using a Ti foil as substrate (denoted as NiFe LDH/Ti).
nodes.source_text: A simple one-step hydrothermal method was carried out to synthesize NiFe LDH using a Ti foil as substrate (denoted as NiFe LDH/Ti).

nodes.source_text: Then the as-prepared NiFe LDH/Ti were irradiated by Ar⁺ ions with a certain energy of 100 keV to different fluences of 1×10¹⁵... (denoted as ir-1e15).

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD pattern of NiFe LDH/Ti matches JPCDS No. 40-0215. After Ar+ irradiation, NiFe LDH peaks decrease and new NiO (200) peak at 2θ=43.2° appears at fluence ≥1×10^16 ions cm^-2; Ni peaks observed at higher fluences.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The XRD pattern of the as-prepared sample matches well with NiFe LDH (JPCDS No. 40–0215)... As the irradiation fluence increases, a new peak at 2θ = 43.2° which assign to the {200} planes of cubic NiO begin to appear...

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM shows uniform nanosheet arrays for as-prepared NiFe LDH/Ti with ~1 μm thickness. After irradiation, nanosheet morphology changes gradually; ir-2e16 largely retains nanosheet structure with increased thickness.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The as-prepared NiFe LDH/Ti shows a uniformly grown nanosheet arrays structure with a film thickness of about 1 um... Typically, it can be seen that the nanosheet structure of the sample ir-2e16 is largely retained, while the thickness of nanosheets increases.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM of as-prepared NiFe LDH shows 0.26 nm interplanar spacing for {012} planes. ir-2e16 shows nanoparticles with 0.21 nm and 0.24 nm for NiO {200}/{111}, 0.20 nm for Ni {111}; crystalline/amorphous heterostructure observed.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) image of the as-prepared catalyst shows the interplanar spacing of 0.26 nm corresponding to the {012} lattice spacing of NiFe LDH... From the HRTEM images of these nanoparticles, the lattice fringes of 0.21 and 0.24 nm belonging to the {200} and {111} crystal planes of cubic NiO... This indicates that crystalline/amorphous heterostructure is formed in the sample ir-2e16.

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman confirms NiFe2O4 phase in irradiated samples with bands at 200, 323, 476, 561, and 681 cm^-1.
nodes.evidence_snippet: After Ar+ ions irradiation, all of the irradiated samples exhibit five Raman bands at 200, 323, 476, 561, and 681 cm^-1, which correspond to the NiFe2O4 phase.

nodes.characterization_summary: Mössbauer spectrum of ir-2e16 at low temperature shows sextet signal similar to pure NiFe2O4, confirming amorphous NiFe2O4 phase.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Mössbauer measurements were further carried out to confirm the existence of the amorphous NiFe2O4 phase... the Mössbauer spectrum of the sample ir-2e16 at low temperature exists a similar sextet signal compared to that of pure NiFe2O4

nodes.characterization_summary: ir-2e16 (NiO/NiFe2O4) exhibits specific surface area of 104.9 m² g^-1 (1.38× higher than NiFe LDH/Ti at 75.9 m² g^-1); type IV isotherm with hysteresis indicates mesopores.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The sample NiO/NiFe2O4 (ir-2e16) exhibits a specific surface area of 104.9 m² g^-1, which is 1.38× higher than that of the as-prepared NiFe LDH/Ti (75.9 m² g^-1).

nodes.characterization_summary: As-prepared NiFe LDH: Ni 2p 856.0/873.6 eV (Ni2+), Fe 2p 712.7 eV (Fe3+), O 1s 531.2/531.9/533.2 eV (M-OH, Ovac, H2O). ir-2e16: Ni 2p metallic 852.7/870.2 eV, Ni2+ -0.5 eV shift, Fe 2p 710.3 eV (Fe3+), O 1s 529.6 eV (lattice oxide), increased Ovac %.
nodes.evidence_snippet: For the as-prepared NiFe LDH/Ti, high-resolution XPS for Ni 2p exists a pair of peaks at 856.0 and 873.6 eV corresponding to Ni 2p3/2 and Ni 2p1/2... the peak at 712.7 eV confirms the presence of Fe3+... After Ar ions irradiation, the Ni2+ peaks... show a 0.5 eV negative shift... new pair of peaks appears at 852.7 and 870.2 eV... new peak at 710.3 eV... new peak at 529.6 eV assigning to metal lattice oxide

nodes.characterization_summary: EPR signals at g=2.00 confirm oxygen vacancies; ir-2e16 shows stronger signal than NiFe LDH/Ti.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spectroscopy further confirmed this conclusion... the signals at g = 2.00 suggest that the structural defects come from oxygen vacancies, and the sample NiO/NiFe2O4 (ir-2e16) shows a stronger signal

nodes.characterization_summary: FT-IR of irradiated samples shows only peaks below 600 cm^-1 (metal-O-metal), confirming break of M-OH bonds.
nodes.evidence_snippet: However, it can be found that only peaks below 600 cm^-1 appear for the irradiated samples, indicating the break of the M-OH bonds during ion irradiation.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM and elemental mapping of ir-2e16 show uniform distribution of elements.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM) image and the corresponding elemental mapping of sample ir-2e16 show uniform distribution of the elements in the sample.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS measurement shows Ni:Fe atom ratio of 2.39:1 in original NiFe LDH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: with atom ratio of 2.39:1 for Ni and Fe basing on EDS measurement, Table S2, Supporting Information
